prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person in Kansas City — the right broker depends on your budget, whether you need help with ACA Marketplace subsidies, whether you want an HSA‑eligible plan, family coverage, or help setting up a QSEHRA, and how much hand‑holding you want year‑round. That said, here’s a practical approach and some concrete next steps so you can find the best fit quickly.

What to look for in a broker (high priority)
- Independent (non‑captive) broker who quotes multiple carriers — you want comparisons, not a single carrier’s pitch.  
- Experience with self‑employed/sole proprietor clients and ACA Marketplace enrollment (subsidies/premium tax credits).  
- Willingness to explain HSA eligibility, QSEHRA or small‑group options, and tax implications.  
- Ongoing service (help with renewals, claims issues) rather than one‑time sales.  
- Clear about fees — most broker compensation comes from carriers, but confirm if they charge client fees.  
- Good reviews or referrals from other freelancers/small‑business owners.

Places to find reputable brokers in Kansas City
- NAHU “Find an Agent” (National Association of Health Underwriters) — search for local certified agents.  
- Missouri Department of Insurance agent lookup to verify license and complaints.  
- Healthcare.gov / Kansas Marketplace certified agents and navigators (free help with Marketplace plans and subsidies).  
- Local resources: Kansas City Chamber of Commerce, SCORE or SBDC — they often have vetted recommendations.  
- Google/Yelp with filters for “independent health insurance broker” + read reviews.

Useful broker types and online options
- Independent local agencies in KC (best for local, personalized service) — look for ones that explicitly list individual/sole proprietor experience.  
- Marketplace‑specialist platforms (HealthSherpa) — good if your priority is ACA plans and subsidies.  
- National comparison sites (eHealth) — quick comparisons across carriers for private plans.  
- Blue Cross & local carrier agents — may be fine if you prefer a single trusted carrier but won’t compare as many options.

Questions to ask a prospective broker
- Which carriers do you represent? Are you independent?  
- How much experience do you have with self‑employed/sole proprietor clients?  
- Can you help me determine Marketplace subsidy eligibility and enroll during Open Enrollment or SEP?  
- Do you help with QSEHRA or small‑group options if I hire employees?  
- Do you charge any fees to clients? What ongoing service do you provide?  
- Can you provide client references?

If you want, I can:
- Search for top‑rated independent health insurance brokers in Kansas City (give me your ZIP code), or  
- Pull together 3–5 local broker names with contact info and recent reviews.

Which would you prefer?
